subject: Re: WillowTech phased swap incentives and ops packaging
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@willowtech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@willowtech.com>, Marta Lopez <m.lopez@willowtech.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: WillowTech RFP — migration incentives and cost alignment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. WillowTech is evaluating a move off our incumbent inference provider and I wanted to start the commercial conversation so procurement and engineering can align. High level context:
- Monthly estimate: ~120M generation tokens, 14M embeddings, peak latency reqs ~150ms P95 for inference.
- Current vendor offers aggressive downward pricing with a migration credit bucket to offset egress/onboarding.

Can Redwood share a commercial framework for:
1) A short-term pilot credit for migration and early ramp (we'd expect a clear cap and milestone releases).
2) Blended committed discounts vs. one-time credits (we're weighing prepay vs. credit structures).
3) Any packaging considerations for a phased swap (pilot -> pilot+dedicated -> full cutover).

Attached is the RFP and usage profile we circulated internally. Procurement will want specifics to map to our cost model.

Appreciate a quick sketch (ballpark is fine) — we need a baseline to include in the vendor comparison matrix by next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships, WillowTech
(415) 555-0193

Attachment: WillowTech_RFP.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@willowtech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WillowTech RFP — migration incentives and cost alignment

Alex — thanks for the RFP and the clear ask. Very interested in working through a phased approach that minimizes risk and keeps runtime economics predictable. Quick sketch below (ballpark figures to start discussion):

Commercial sketch (pilot -> phased swap -> scale):
- Pilot (6–8 weeks): consumption credit covering onboarding + pilot run up to $60k (applied to hosted usage).
- Phased swap (first 3 months post-pilot): milestone-tied onboarding credit up to $75k (released 25% on go-live, 75% after validation of latency/KPIs).
- Scale price options: 8–12% committed discount on standard hosted rates for a 12mo commitment; alternative is a 5% discount + $120k upfront credit applied against usage in year 1.

Operational support and packaging:
- Two-week Dedicated onboarding bootcamp (technical runbook, KV cache tuning, prefix caching setup).
- Optional Dedicated pool with guaranteed concurrency if you want strict latency SLAs — pricing for Dedicated would be quoted after workload validation.

We can also structure a blended approach: smaller upfront credit + smaller committed discount (helps align incentives). For procurement, I can map how credits interact with billing (credits reduce invoiced usage; we can allow partial rollover for the pilot window).

Next steps: I attached a short SOW that outlines the pilot scope and success criteria. If you can flag three must-have integration/egress concerns, Rishi and I will produce a tighter term sheet and a DocuSign-ready MSA amendment.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Willow_WarmUp_Pilot_SOW.pdf
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@willowtech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@willowtech.com>, Marta Lopez <m.lopez@willowtech.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WillowTech RFP — migration incentives and cost alignment

Lauren — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering after reviewing the SOW:

Procurement asks:
- Can the onboarding credit be structured as a milestone pool that releases against measurable runtime deltas (so we only pay net if the actual savings are realized)?
- If we do the upfront credit + discount route, what are the termination tranches (we need protections if we decommit early).

Engineering asks:
- Can you quantify the Dedicated bootcamp deliverables (do you run perf tests in our staging? who owns the runbook?).
- We need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short note on data residency / log retention for PII-sensitive workloads.

Commercial ask: given our incumbent is offering a 30% first-year migration credit (structured as consumption rebate + professional services waiver), would Redwood consider a hybrid: 12% committed discount + a $90k milestone-tracked migration stipend that can be reallocated to PS if unused?

I attached an annotated RFP with in-line notes. Procurement wants a DocuSign-ready term sheet they can share internally once we have numbers.

Thanks — Alex

Attachment: Willow_RFP_annotated.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@willowtech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WillowTech RFP — migration incentives and cost alignment

Alex — looping in a tighter commercial counter to move procurement toward an executable term sheet. Appreciate the annotated RFP — that made the asks clear.

Redwood counter (proposal v1):
- Migration stipend: $90,000 total milestone pool. Release schedule: 25% on signed SOW, 35% on pilot success (latency and correctness KPIs met), 40% on initial production cutover + verification (30 days). Stipend can be reallocated to professional services if requested by WillowTech.
- Committed pricing: 12% discount on hosted list rates for a 12-month commitment at the forecasted volume, with a configurable true-up at quarter boundaries. Alternatively, a 7% discount + $120k prepaid credit applied to year 1 usage.
- Dedicated onboarding: we run perf benchmarks in your staging (joint tests), deliver a deployment runbook and caching config; bootcamp includes two onsite/remote workshops.
- Termination/early decommit: credits apply only to invoiced usage; if WillowTech terminates early, remaining committed discount periods convert to a true-up at list rates for used capacity. Exact termination tranches will be in the MSA addendum.

Compliance: we will provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and a summary of retention options (we can offer account-level log retention controls and can scope a private deployment for stricter residency needs).

Next steps:
1) Lauren/Marissa — finalize a one-page term sheet with the stipend release language so Alex can present to procurement.
2) Alex — confirm whether Willow wants the $90k stipend as pure consumption credit or split PS/credit.
3) We will push a DocuSign-ready term sheet and HubSpot deal update (HubSpot: deal/12457890).

I'll attach the migration-credit terms doc for legal to review.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
